messages:
alex_peopleops: Quick case for payroll/tax help  Diego converted from contractor to FT effective 2025-10-03. We ended up with two separate payments: contractor invoice in USD and first salary run in EUR. Withholdings look inconsistent and benefits need retro enrollment. Can payroll + tax advise on remediations?

sam_payroll: Can you drop the payrun/invoice IDs and gross numbers so I can pull records?

alex_peopleops: Invoice: INV-2025-1098-DG gross USD 9,200. Salary payrun: PR-2025-10-08-FT-DG gross EUR 5,100 (pro-rated). Diego relocated to Ireland 2025-10-03.

sam_payroll: Our systems flagged a 1099 issued under the US entity and a W-2 processed under the EU payroll. @lina_tax can Irish residency change retro to 10/1 affect whether we should cancel/adjust the 1099?

lina_tax: It depends. If the contractor work on the invoice was physically performed in the US, issuing a 1099 is defensible. If services were performed after relocation or remotely from IE, we should reclassify for local payroll and consider 1099-c + W-2. Need supporting docs: travel dates, signed statement, and offer letter. Also check any tax treaty implications.

diego_engineer: I was in SF through 10/2 and flew to Dublin 10/3 AM. Invoice covers work through 10/2. My FT start day was 10/3 and subsequent work happened in Ireland.

marie_finance: From an accounting perspective, invoice covers pre-relocation US work; salary covers EU employment. We should avoid duplicate reporting for the same services. Two paths: (A) keep 1099 for the invoice (US-sourced) + W-2 for FT salary, ensure no overlapping withholding; (B) reclassify contractor payment into payroll and issue corrected forms. Lina, which is cleaner compliance-wise?

lina_tax: Cleaner and lower risk is to document the split: 1099 for pre-conversion US work (9/29-10/2) and payroll for post-conversion EU wages (from 10/3). That requires travel docs and affirmation from Diego that invoice covers work done in US. If any doubt, reclassification may be necessary. Also ensure Irish PAYE applies to W-2 wages and no US withholding on same earnings.

alex_peopleops: Action items please?

sam_payroll: I'll: 1) verify which entity issued the 1099; 2) check withholding flags on the W-2 run; 3) open a payroll ops ticket to tag runs so year-end reporting is accurate. Will also confirm whether we need to issue a 1099-C or W-2c.

payroll_bot: Check complete  1099 issued under US EIN 12-3456789 for INV-2025-1098-DG. W-2 issued under Irish payroll umbrella for PR-2025-10-08-FT-DG. No US withholding was applied on the W-2.

sam_payroll: Good. Marie, can finance handle FX adjustment and ensure benefits premiums are backdated to 10/3 for pro-rated employer contributions?

marie_finance: Yes, I'll coordinate with benefits vendor and accounting. Will confirm whether employer premium should be pro-rated for Oct and post any GL adjustments.

alex_peopleops: Diego, please upload travel itinerary and signed contractor invoice to support keeping the 1099. Lina  any other doc we should ask for?

lina_tax: Please provide travel itinerary showing US presence through 10/2, contractor statement confirming services/dates, and the signed offer letter with FT start 10/3. That substantiates the split. If anything missing, we should prepare to reclassify and issue corrective filings.

diego_engineer: Uploaded flight receipt + itinerary and invoice to our payroll file share: https://files.redwood/payroll/diego/relocate. Also attached the signed offer.

sam_payroll: Received. Logging ticket PAY-4521 to mark runs and attach docs. I'll update once ops flags the transactions and confirms whether a 1099-C is needed or if we can leave as-is.

alex_peopleops: Thanks everyone. Please post updates here. If a corrected form is needed let's coordinate before year-end so employee has correct documentation for filing. :thumbsup:
